evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.

criteria.reasoning: The rationale and users (marine scientists) are clearly identified, benefiting the Great Barrier Reef. However, formal engineering requirements (e.g., revisit rate, spectral bands, spatial resolution) are absent.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart. Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page.

criteria.reasoning: A Gantt chart and task breakdowns are provided, linking back to the mission stages. However, contingencies, risk mitigation, and project variation planning are missing.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, in my progress, I have read the brief of Asner’s monitoring system in Hawaii, researched into how coral bleaching occurs and its severity, and also completed STK tutorials 1, 2, 3 & 4.

criteria.reasoning: There is virtually no actual preliminary technical output (no preliminary orbit calculations, constellation analysis, or STK outputs), only a statement that tutorials were completed.
The report has a neat layout and readable prose, but referencing consists entirely of bare URLs rather than formal bibliographic citations.

technical_issues.issue: Leaving an Earth-observation satellite 'where it is' at end-of-life violates standard space debris mitigation guidelines (e.g. 25-year de-orbit rule in LEO).

overall: Good conceptual foundation and a clear Gantt chart, but technical progress is lacking: no engineering analysis, orbit calculations, or STK figures are included.
